META.subject: General Science
META.titleDoc: GENERAL SCIENCE GRADE 10: TURNING EFFECT OF FORCE
META.subtitleDoc: OpenAI-only evaluation • Sub-Strand 3.1 • 12 lessons • teacher review copy

UNIT.sep: Model force geometry,calculate signed moments,compare pivots and record actual versus supplied evidence.
UNIT.careers: Illustrative mechanical design,maintenance and scientific measurement roles.
UNIT.focus: Moments of a force at a point; Moments of anti-parallel forces; Applications of the turning effect of force in real life.
UNIT.phenomenon: A fictional tool poster claims every force creates a moment and every equal opposite force pair is fully balanced.
UNIT.supportingPhenomena: Explicit force-position records,conditional metre-rule balancing,couple/unequal-pair comparisons and safe application observations.
UNIT.drivingQuestion: How is the turning effect of force used in our daily life?
UNIT.content: Moments of a force at a point; Moments of anti-parallel forces; Applications of the turning effect of force in real life.
UNIT.coreCompetencies:
Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner solves numerical problems involving both moments of a force and moments of anti-parallel forces and identifies areas where moments of a force is used in day-to-day life.
Digital literacy: as the learner interacts with digital technology when researching on moments of a force at a point and moments of anti-parallel forces.
UNIT.values:
Integrity: the learner displays honesty while using digital devices to search for information on moments of a force at a point and moments of anti-parallel forces.
Respect: the learner respects others’ opinions while discussing with peers on the examples involving turning effect of force in daily life.
UNIT.pcis: Life skills (self-awareness): as the learner demonstrates the principle of moments of force by balancing a metre rule.
UNIT.subject: General Science
UNIT.learningOutcomes:
determine moments of a force at a point,
calculate the moments of anti-parallel forces,
apply the turning effect of force in real-life situations,
appreciate the importance of the turning effect of force in everyday life.

FINAL_EXPLANATION.instructions: Independent40minutes:4readTF12,10Section1,12Section2,8Section3,6Section4/check/submit. Use only final reference/prompts;no hints or keys. Draw force diagrams and show contributions with units/turning sense. No actual practical or digital action is inferred.

sections.title: 1. Moments and perpendicular distances
sections.prompt: Draw CaseA force lines and pivot from TF12. Calculate signed moment for the downward force,magnitude for the slant force and moment for the line-through-pivot force. Explain why the slant turning sense is unknown and why a general handle length is not always the lever arm.
sections.exemplar: Down10N at+0.24m gives−2.4N m clockwise. Through-pivot line gives0. Slant magnitude12×0.15=1.8N m;no arrow sense supplied,so its turning sense is undetermined. Use shortest perpendicular pivot-to-line distance,not arbitrary application distance. Actual diagrams required.

sections.title: 2. Anti-parallel pairs and pivot choice
sections.prompt: For CaseB find resultant force and net moment about both O andP,showing separate signed contributions. Verify the couple formula using line separation. For CaseC find resultant force and moment about O;explain why it is not a pure couple.
sections.exemplar: B resultant0. O:+1.5+0.5=+2.0N m. P:−1.0+3.0=+2.0N m. Separation0.40m×5N=2.0N m,counterclockwise. C resultant2N up;O:+0.6+0.5=+1.1N m. Unequal pair has nonzero resultant,not a pure couple;moment need not be pivot-independent.

sections.title: 3. Balance and application
sections.prompt: For CaseD draw all forces and find F and pivot reaction for static balance. Calculate the door force for the given required moment and arm. Explain one condition or practical limit on applying the door/tool model.
sections.exemplar: Moment balance2×0.25=F×0.10 givesF5N. Force balance requires upward reaction7N;reaction acts through pivot. Door6/0.75=8N perpendicular. Actual product/stability/clearance/friction conditions require checking;no improvised extensions or force trial is authorised.

sections.title: 4. Daily-use explanation and evidence scope
sections.prompt: Explain another everyday turning-effect use with pivot,force direction and arm identified. State a useful benefit and limit. Explain why zero net moment alone is insufficient for full static equilibrium and whether these written records prove actual balancing,walking or digital actions.
sections.exemplar: A handle/scissors/tap example identifies geometry and useful leverage/controlled turning with product/safety limits. Static balance also needs zero resultant force. Supplied calculations do not prove actual metre-rule demonstration,school walk or animation use;separate observations are needed.

lessons.title: How do force direction and position set turning sense?

lessons.learned: Clockwise/anticlockwise sense depends on pivot,force position and direction.
lessons.explained: Does every downward force turn clockwise? Include the relevant pivot and evidence limit.

lessons.title: What conditions balance an ideal bar?

lessons.explained: What changes if the bar is not weightless? Include the relevant pivot and evidence limit.

lessons.title: Why can equal opposite forces still turn a body?

lessons.explained: Does zero resultant force imply zero turning effect? Include the relevant pivot and evidence limit.

lessons.title: When are anti-parallel forces not a couple?
